question: What type of reaction occurs when barium chloride reacts with sodium sulfate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Double displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Double displacement reaction:** A chemical reaction in which two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds is called a double displacement reaction. This typically occurs in aqueous solutions.
 
• **Reaction of barium chloride with sodium sulfate:** When barium chloride (BaCl₂) reacts with sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄), a double displacement reaction takes place, leading to the formation of barium sulfate (BaSO₄) and sodium chloride (NaCl).
 
• **Reaction equation:** BaCl₂(aq) + Na₂SO₄(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq). This equation clearly shows the exchange of ions between the reactants.
 
• **Barium sulfate precipitate:** BaSO₄ is insoluble in water and precipitates out of the solution, making this reaction a classic example of a precipitation reaction as well.
 
• **Applications:** Such double displacement reactions are widely used in qualitative analysis to identify the presence of certain ions in a solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Double displacement reaction characteristics:**

 
 
• Occurs between two ionic compounds in an aqueous solution.
 
• Involves the exchange of ions between the reactants.
 
• Can result in the formation of a precipitate, gas, or a weak electrolyte.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation reaction:** A type of double displacement reaction where an insoluble solid (precipitate) forms and separates out from the solution. Example: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl.
 
• **Other types of reactions:**
 
 
• **Decomposition reaction:** A single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. Example: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
 
• **Combination reaction:** Two or more substances combine to form a single product. Example: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
 
• **Oxidation reaction:** A reaction involving the loss of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion. Example: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
 
 
 
• **Practical significance:** Double displacement reactions are used in various industries, including:
 
 
• **Pharmaceuticals:** For drug synthesis and purification processes.
 
• **Water treatment:** Removal of unwanted ions by precipitation.
 
• **Qualitative analysis:** Identification of specific ions in a solution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of solubility rules:** The solubility rules help predict whether a precipitate will form in a double displacement reaction. For instance, BaSO₄ is insoluble in water, leading to precipitation.
 
• **Testing for sulfate ions:** The formation of BaSO₄ as a white precipitate when BaCl₂ is added to a solution is a common test for the presence of sulfate ions.
 
• **Environmental relevance:** Precipitation reactions are used to remove harmful ions (e.g., heavy metals) from wastewater to make it environmentally safe.
 
• **Limitations:** Double displacement reactions generally occur in an aqueous medium, and the reactants must be soluble for the reaction to proceed efficiently.
